title: Week of Aug 31 – Sep 6
subtitle: Block 3, Big-4 retest — Week 3, the push week. Full frame is back: lower Mon · quality run Tue · upper Wed · easy run Thu · full body Fri · calisthenics Sat · jog + strides Sun. No ride this week — the miles come back on foot. Deload + 5K TT next week.
goals: Retest week. Every number is on the table off last week's log: Squat 205×5 (Block 1's best was 200×5 — you called 195 easy and said you had room, so take it), Bench 190×5 (you jumped the plan and hit 185 on a hot day after a long ride — 190 matches the Block 1 best and beats it on reps), Deadlift 275×4 (ties the Block 1 number), strict OHP 120×5 (115 moved last week; 120 is the 0.65×BW marker on the fitness list). Top sets at ~2 RIR, unspotted bench rules, full back protocol on every hinge. Next week is the deload — there is no week 4 to save it for.

Running: no ride this week per your call, so the aerobic work comes back on foot and both speed and volume step up — 19.5 planned miles (Mon 1.5 + Tue 6.5 + Thu 5.5 + Fri 2.5 + Sun 3.5) vs last week's 15, holding the block's ~20 flat. Two quality touches: Tuesday grows to 4×6 min at threshold (you said the 3×6 felt so much better and the reps ran long anyway — the fitness is coming back), and Thursday's easy run finishes with ~1.5 mi steady Z3 to replace the ride tempo as the second touch. Roughly 40 hard minutes on ~3 aerobic hours — the 70/30 lane.

Strength volume: also up, per your call. Saturday calisthenics returns now that the travel weekend is done — that's the fourth strength day back, and the max pull-up benchmark moves there with it (still the morning after a lift day, so 15 stays comparable). ~78 planned sets on the week vs ~73 last week, everything inside the 75–90 build band.

Core, rebuilt the way you asked: nothing but you and the floor — no cables, no wheel, no bands, no bar, no dumbbell to hunt down. Still 6+ sets every lift day, still rotated: Mon = dead bug / bicycle crunch / plank, Wed = hollow hold / V-up / side plank, Fri (deadlift day, spine-friendly) = side plank / dead bug / bird dog, Sat = plank shoulder taps / hollow hold / flutter kicks. Grab-and-go circuits, 20s between moves.

Two log notes carried in: barbell row stays at 135 (your call — 'stick to 135 next week'), and leg curls stay in for single-leg glute bridges since that fit the gym setup better. Friday's easy-run discipline note: last Friday averaged 160 — this week's easy miles mean ≤150, and the steady finish is the only part allowed above it.
Food: maintenance, deficit 0, band 189–191, waist is the arbiter. You're attempting four rep-PRs in five days — eat like it. Waist measurement Sunday morning, fasted.
review: Week 2 did exactly what a push week should. Squat 195×5 with room ('I will have room to move up next week' — quoted, and honored Monday). RDL 205×8 at the edge you wanted. Bench you took to 185 past the plan's 180, on a warm evening AFTER a 40.55-mile ride — that ride, by the way, was the biggest of the year and your Tuesday journal said the intervals finally felt like yours again. Deadlift 265×4 clean the morning after those bike miles. Pull-up benchmark 15, up from 14 under identical conditions, so the trend is real. The guaranteed 17 became 15 running miles when travel ate the flex run — that's what the guarantee was for, and this week rebuilds it. One honest flag: Friday's 'easy' 7.5 averaged 160 again. This week the retest tops take everything you've got, which is exactly why the easy miles have to actually be easy.

days.name: Quality Run — 4×6 Threshold
warmup: 2×20s relaxed strides before the first rep

run.title: Cruise Intervals — 4×6 min, 6.5 mi total
run.detail: 1.5 mi easy warm-up → 4 × 6 min at threshold effort (comfortably hard — short sentences, not gasps) with 2 min easy jog between → easy cool-down to round out 6.5. The fourth rep is the progression: last week you said it felt so much better, the reps ran long on their own, and the limiter was squat-day legs, not lungs. Same legs situation today (retest squat yesterday), so same assignment: start rep 1 slower than feels right, finish every rep able to do one more. Your HR read from last week was correct — mid-170s is right for 6-min reps; don't chase the 180s, that's 5K effort, not threshold.
